behavior: Shift+Tab in the popup of a menu or a select asks for the close with the reason `focus-out`. When a handler cancels the close, the popup stays open, and the focus still goes to the trigger. In a submenu, the focus goes to the submenu trigger, or to the input of a filterable parent menu. From the input of a filterable menu, the focus goes to the trigger. The store of a root context menu has no trigger element, so a canceled close for Tab or Shift+Tab keeps the focus in its modal popup. In Base UI, Shift+Tab does nothing when the close is canceled: the list stops the key and moves no focus. Tab still leaves the popup, so the focus can leave in one direction only.
